source: the selection rule (the model ladder measures only task complexity; models are chosen by the benchmark classifiers of the task): a model without data in a classifier of the task takes the nearest classifier, marked as a substitute and counted as coverage; without any, no automatic assignment and a question to the operator. The rows are the initial table of the design analysis of that rule.
rules: A row names one registry ID (dimension) and its nearest classifiers in order (nearest). A selection that finds no comparable cell of the model in the dimension takes the first nearest ID in which the model has one, marks the score as a substitute of that ID and counts the dimension as covered. One step only: the nearest ID of a nearest ID is never taken. Every ID is a registry ID that is not a crosswalk label, the quarantine bucket or a removed ID; a dimension never names itself; a dimension without a row has no substitute. basis says why the IDs are near.

rows.basis: the three coding IDs of one split coding dimension: swe-bench families (D-IMPL), aider-polyglot (D-EDIT) and the code generation families (D-ALGO) all score written code
review and critique are the certification pair of the registry; the implementation strength is the reviewer proxy the selection layer used before, now marked
